For Q4, adjusted comparable sales growth is projected to be largely stable versus Q3, as per Bay Area Ideas. However, margin risks are heightened by tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty, the analyst added.
With the wholesale retailer’s top-line performance largely priced in, investors will be turning their attention to its membership trends.

“I expect FY26 membership fees to come close to $6B, with accrued rewards to be around $3B. Gross membership income should then be $9B; divided by an estimated 84.3M paid members, we have gross income per member of $106.76, which is an 8% YoY growth. These are solid figures, which is what Costco usually reports,” Seeking Alpha analyst Luca Socci said in a recent article.

Another key area of interest is expected to be the firm’s cash position, as per the analyst, on hopes of an upcoming special dividend—which it announces every 2 to 3 years during its Q1 results as a 'Christmas Present'.
“Costco is quite close to a cash position of $20B, and I am almost 100% positive that once Costco reports, we will see it sitting on top of roughly $22B, if not $23B, in cash,” Socci said.
“My last estimate is that the special dividend may be roughly $20, but given the company's recent growth trajectory, I would not be surprised to see it around $21 or $22,” he added.
